name: The Blackwood Corrupted
summary: In northern Darkshore, the Blackwood Corrupted are caught in a dark influence. Evidence in the tainted waters of Cliffspring River leads Thundris Windweaver to send you against it. You gather their food and purify it with moonwell water, drawing the demonic handler into the open and breaking his hold on the northern camp.

sections.title: A Hidden Master
sections.body: In Auberdine, the night elves have long wondered why the once-peaceful Blackwood furbolgs turned on their neighbors. Their search along Cliffspring River traced the rot to satyr meddling. These ancient servants of the Burning Legion manipulate the tribe with fel magic. Insidious talismans twist the furbolgs' minds and drive them into feral aggression.

sections.title: Breaking the Shackles
sections.body: Thundris Windweaver prepares a remedy to draw the puppet master out. You gather grain, fruit, and nuts from the northern Blackwood settlement, then soak them in holy water from Auberdine's moonwell. The water purifies the tainted food. Set it by the central bonfire, and nearby furbolgs find brief respite from madness. Xabraxxis, the satyr corruptor, emerges in fury to defend his hold over the camp.

faq.q: Why are the Blackwood furbolgs aggressive?
faq.answer: The furbolgs' minds have been poisoned by demonic influence. Satyrs secretly planted themselves near the camps and channel foul magic through enchanted talismans. This twists the furbolgs' natural instincts into rabid violence.

Xabraxxis is a satyr corruptor who oversees the northern Blackwood furbolg camp. He works from the shadows to keep the tribe gripped by fel madness, using a Talisman of Corruption to sustain his control.

faq.q: Does cleansing their food cure the furbolgs forever?
faq.answer: No. Moonwell-infused food breaks the demonic haze only long enough for the furbolgs to know peace and draw out Xabraxxis. Slaying the satyr and claiming his talisman is a significant victory, but Thundris Windweaver says a permanent cure for the corrupted tribes will take more effort.

faq.q: Where did the idea to use moonwell water come from?
faq.answer: Moonwells are sacred pools blessed by the Goddess Elune. Their rejuvenating magic counters fel and undeath. Thundris Windweaver provides a cleansing bowl so the sanctified water can neutralize the demonic toxins woven into the furbolgs' food.

faq.q: What happens when the food bowl is placed at the bonfire?
faq.answer: The nearby furbolgs briefly break free of their bloodlust. They gather peacefully around the blessed food and stop attacking. Enraged that his puppets are escaping their torment, Xabraxxis appears at once to punish the meddlers.

Thundris Windweaver is a night elf researcher and investigator stationed in Auberdine. He coordinates efforts to uncover the causes of Darkshore's creeping ecological decay and the madness gripping local wildlife.

angles.text: The furbolgs were long friends of the kaldorei. Seeing them fall under the sway of their ancestral enemies, the satyrs, is a bitter tragedy night elves are eager to set right.
Restoring balance means cutting out the rot at its root. A satyr's fel talismans warp primal woodland creatures, making the Cenarion Circle's confrontation with Xabraxxis urgent.
Channeling Elune's pure, restorative grace through moonwell water stands in stark contrast to the corrupting shadow and fel magic the satyr wields.
